evidence: Across all languages, 145 human annotators were asked to score all 1,888 pairs (in their given language). We finally collect at least ten valid annotations for each word pair in each language. All annotators were required to abide by the following instructions:

1. Each annotator must assign an integer score between 0 and 6 (inclusive) indicating how semantically similar the two words in a given pair are. A score of 6 indicates very high similarity (i.e., perfect synonymy), while zero indicates no similarity.
2. Each annotator must score the entire set of 1,888 pairs in the dataset. The pairs must not be shared between different annotators.
3. Annotators are able to break the workload over a period of approximately 2-3 weeks, and are able to use external sources (e.g. dictionaries, thesauri, WordNet) if required.
4. Annotators are kept anonymous, and are not able to communicate with each other during the annotation process.

title: Multi-SimLex: A Large-Scale Evaluation of Multilingual and Cross-Lingual Lexical Semantic Similarity
answer_short: 145 human annotators were asked to score all 1,888 pairs in their given language, with at least ten valid annotations per pair, following a three-round adjudication protocol to ensure quality.
answer_rationale: The annotation process involved 145 human annotators who scored each of the 1,888 word pairs in their respective languages, with at least ten valid annotations per pair. The process followed a three-round adjudication protocol: Round 1 involved initial scoring; Round 2 involved re-evaluation of the most disagreed-upon pairs; and Round 3 involved discarding annotators with the lowest agreement scores while maintaining at least ten annotators per language. This protocol ensured quality and consistency in the annotations.
